title: For a surjective open continuous map the closures, closed sets, opens and locally closed sets are exactly the preimages

standard_prerequisites.name: The behaviour of closures under a continuous map, and the definition of a submersive map as one whose target carries the quotient topology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on submersive maps, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the four numbered assertions and the notion of submersiveness in the final sentence.

core_obligations: Part (1): the inclusion of the closure of the preimage in the preimage of the closure is immediate; for the reverse inclusion the proof takes a point outside the closure of the preimage, uses an open neighbourhood of it missing the preimage, and the openness of the map to produce an open neighbourhood of its image missing T (proof lines 785-790).
Parts (2) and (3): the characterisations of closed and open subsets follow from part (1) together with the openness of the map and the surjectivity (proof lines 790-795).
Part (4): local closedness is reduced to openness of T inside its closure using the map restricted to the closure of the preimage, which is again open onto its image (proof lines 795-797).
Conclusion: the four assertions, and hence that the surjective open continuous map is submersive (proof line 797).
proof_roadmap: (1) 先得 cl(f^{-1}T) ⊂ f^{-1}(cl T)；反向取闭包外的点，用开邻域与 f 的开性得到 f(x) 的开邻域不交 T。
(2)(3) 由 (1) 与开性、满射性直接得到；(4) 把 T 在 cl T 中的开性用限制到 cl(f^{-1}T) 上的映射来判，最后得 f 是 submersive。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the list of exactness properties of a surjective open continuous map (author lemma at source lines 770-782, label lemma-open-morphism-quotient-topology): preimages commute with closures, and closedness, openness and local closedness of subsets of the target are tested on preimages, which in particular makes the map submersive. The proof (source lines 784-798) proves the closure statement by an explicit point argument in which the openness of the map is what lets one push an open neighbourhood forward (proof lines 785-790), and then derives the other three from it, using the restriction to the closure of the preimage for the locally closed case (proof lines 795-797). H2.
